text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-71234 — capacity_exhaustion on service=inference-queue (severity: P1). Alerts: pending_requests > 10k for 3m, queue_latency p95 > 6s. Auto-escalation in 5m if unacknowledged.

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident created: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-71234 — page routed to eng-oncall rotation.

Maria Chen: on call — acknowledging. I'm pulling autoscaler and node-group metrics now.

Jason Lee: I can see a sustained ramp from a few customers — bursts to 12k concurrent tokens. Autoscaler target nodes increased but new nodes are stuck in Provisioning state. Cloud API errors: "Insufficient quota: GPUs" in the recent events.

Priya Singh: @Maria do we have spare burst capacity in Dedicated pools? Any fallback routing configured?

Maria Chen: Dedicated pool shows 0 spare nodes. Fallback policy currently set to best-effort on smaller model variant but that path is hitting memory OOMs. Customer impact: some requests are queued >30s, visible 502s at the edge. Initial estimate: ~6-10% of requests affected, mostly long-sequence batch jobs.

Kevin O'Neil: I'm checking cloud quota dashboards — looks like a sudden supplier-side quota enforcement in region us-west2. We can request emergency quota but that takes time. Short-term: manual scale of lighter worker class and enable KV-prefetch to reduce warmup.

Jason Lee: Trying a manual replica bump on the shared pool to soak traffic into smaller models. Command: 

```
# scale down heavy-gpu pool and scale up cpu-backed workers
kubectl scale --replicas=12 deploy/inference-cpu-workers -n prod
kubectl scale --replicas=2 deploy/inference-gpu-heavy -n prod
```

Maria Chen: Executing now. Also flipping prefix cache TTL to aggressive warmup: 

```
# enable aggressive kvcache warmup for hot prefixes
redwoodctl config set kvcache.hot_warmup=true --service inference-queue
```

incident-bot: Action log: Manual scaling commands executed by Maria Chen.

Priya Singh: After the scale to cpu workers, p95 latency dropped to ~2.8s for streaming requests, pending_requests halved. We're still seeing failures for long-seq requests that require GPU.

SRE Pager: @Maria @Jason we've got to coordinate a handoff if this is still unstable in 20m. Suggest we open a PD mitigation playbook: throttle long sequences, apply queuing caps, and notify customers.

Maria Chen: Agreed. Steps I'm proposing now: 1) Keep cpu-backed workers up to absorb short/medium requests 2) Apply request-size-based routing to divert seq_len>2048 to a degraded path with async retry 3) Request emergency GPU quota from cloud and engage infra on vendor channel.

Kevin O'Neil: Filing emergency quota request now (req: +10 GPUs in us-west2). Also standing up a temporary spot pool in us-east1 and preparing cross-region routing if quota remains blocked.

Jason Lee: Putting a short-lived circuit breaker on model=large-gen for new sessions to prevent more long-seq churn: 

```
# set route-level rate limit
redwoodctl routes update inference-large --rate-limit 50rps --circuit-breaker 5m
```

Maria Chen: Notifying product/sales with initial customer impact note. Copying the incident summary to #incidents.

Maria Chen: Customer impact summary (to be posted): ~6-10% user-facing errors/latency spikes, mostly batch/long-sequence traffic. Mitigations in flight: manual CPU scaling, kvcache warmup, route throttles, emergency quota request. Next update in 10m or on escalation.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by Maria Chen (eng-oncall). Escalation paused.

incident-bot: Reminder: if PD not resolved in 20m, will auto-escalate to senior oncall and exec notify.

SRE Pager: I'm taking the 3:00–3:30 handoff if this continues — @Maria please DM any partial playbook notes. I'll be on standby.

Priya Singh: Quick check — any customer-facing mitigation messages drafted? We should warn enterprise customers in the affected region.

Maria Chen: Drafting a short message now and will ping support to send to active sessions / webhook customers.

Kevin O'Neil: Cloud quota request submitted (ticket# Q-33845). Vendor chat initiated. If we get +5 GPUs in 10–15m we can bring enough heavy workers up to fully mitigate.

Jason Lee: Metrics trending: pending_requests from 11.2k -> 4.9k over 8m after changes, error rate decreasing. Keeping an eye on requeue loops.

incident-bot: PD-71234 — update logged. Next update scheduled in 10 minutes or on status change.

Maria Chen: Summary update for thread: manual mitigations reduced immediate customer impact, root cause suspected sudden capacity quota enforcement combined with a warmup pattern in a few heavy users. Handoff intent: if still unstable at 1765440199 (20m from now) escalate to SRE Pager for mitigation and exec notif.

SRE Pager: Acknowledged — will pick up if needed. tagging for postmortem: autoscaler warmup behavior, pre-warm policy, cross-region fallback automation. :clipboard: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
